content.overview: Tort liability may be discharged by death where the claim is personal and not saved by statute, by accord and satisfaction, release, judgment, limitation or another recognised legal event.
content.glance: Tort liability may be discharged by death where the claim is personal and not saved by statute, by accord and satisfaction, release, judgment, limitation or another recognised legal event.
content.study: Tort liability may be discharged by death where the claim is personal and not saved by statute, by accord and satisfaction, release, judgment, limitation or another recognised legal event.\n\nThe historical actio personalis rule was modified by Indian legislation. Settlement and release, merger in judgment and limitation may also extinguish or bar claims. Discharge is distinct from a defence on the merits.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: The historical actio personalis rule was modified by Indian legislation. Settlement and release, merger in judgment and limitation may also extinguish or bar claims. Discharge is distinct from a defence on the merits.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: The consequences are shaped by common law, Limitation Act 1963, procedural rules, contractual release and survival statutes. A release should be construed according to its terms.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. Identify existing cause. 2. Identify alleged extinguishing event. 3. Determine whether it legally discharges the claim. 4. Check statutory exceptions and surviving causes. 5. Prevent double recovery.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: Release deeds, settlement agreements, judgments, payment records and correspondence may prove discharge. The party relying on discharge should establish the instrument or event.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Raise discharge specifically with the relevant instrument and chronology. Limitation is separately analysed. The court should determine the actual scope of a release.

examples.body: The effect of death and survival depends on the statutory character of the claim; not every tort action is extinguished by death.

examples.title: Illustration 2 — Boundary Defect
examples.body: Indian survival statutes modify the historical common-law rule.
